english: Let $C$ be the circle $(z-1-2i)(\bar{z}-7+10i)+(\bar{z}-1+2i)(z-7-10i)=0$ in the Argand plane, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Suppose that $C$ is also the locus of the points $z$ satisfying $|z-\alpha|=k|z-5-6i|$ for a complex number $\alpha$ and a real number $k>1$. Then the value of $|\alpha|^{2}+k^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $C$ आर्गण्ड तल में वृत्त $(z-1-2i)(\bar{z}-7+10i)+(\bar{z}-1+2i)(z-7-10i)=0$ है, जहाँ $i=\sqrt{-1}$ है। मान लीजिए कि $C$, किसी सम्मिश्र संख्या $\alpha$ तथा वास्तविक संख्या $k>1$ के लिए $|z-\alpha|=k|z-5-6i|$ को संतुष्ट करने वाले बिन्दुओं $z$ का बिन्दुपथ भी है। तब $|\alpha|^{2}+k^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $(z-z_{1})(\bar{z}-\bar{z}_{2})+(\bar{z}-\bar{z}_{1})(z-z_{2})=0$ with $z_{1}=1+2i$, $z_{2}=7+10i$ is the diametric form: $C$ has centre $c=4+6i$, radius $R=\dfrac{|6+8i|}{2}=5$
For $|z-\alpha|=k|z-\beta|$ the centre is $c=\dfrac{\alpha-k^{2}\beta}{1-k^{2}}$, which gives $\alpha-c=k^{2}(\beta-c)$, and $R=\dfrac{k|\alpha-\beta|}{k^{2}-1}=k|\beta-c|$
solution_full: The equation says $\mathrm{Re}\left[(z-z_{1})\overline{(z-z_{2})}\right]=0$ with $z_{1}=1+2i$, $z_{2}=7+10i$, i.e. the vectors from $z_{1}$ and $z_{2}$ to $z$ are perpendicular. So $C$ is the circle on the segment from $z_{1}$ to $z_{2}$ as diameter: centre $c=4+6i$, radius $R=\dfrac{|z_{2}-z_{1}|}{2}=\dfrac{|6+8i|}{2}=5$.

Squaring $|z-\alpha|^{2}=k^{2}|z-\beta|^{2}$ (with $\beta=5+6i$) gives $(k^{2}-1)|z|^{2}-2\mathrm{Re}\left(z\,\overline{(k^{2}\beta-\alpha)}\right)+k^{2}|\beta|^{2}-|\alpha|^{2}=0$, a circle with centre $c=\dfrac{k^{2}\beta-\alpha}{k^{2}-1}$.

Hence $\alpha-c=k^{2}\beta-(k^{2}-1)c-c=k^{2}(\beta-c)$ and $\beta-c=\dfrac{\beta-\alpha}{1-k^{2}}$. The radius is $R=\dfrac{k|\alpha-\beta|}{k^{2}-1}=k|\beta-c|$, and $|\alpha-c|\,|\beta-c|=R^{2}$ ($\alpha,\beta$ are inverse points of $C$).
originality_note: New: a circle given in diametric form is rewritten as an Apollonius circle with a prescribed second point; alpha is the inverse point of beta and k = R/|beta - c| (way 3, an object fixed by two conditions). Closest known: centre and radius of |z - a| = k|z - b|. Different because: the direction is reversed: the circle and one point are given, and the other point and the ratio are recovered.
blueprint_concepts: Circle in complex form; Apollonius locus |z-z1|/|z-z2| = k

concept_use.Circle in complex form; Apollonius locus: The centre (alpha - k^2 beta)/(1 - k^2) and radius k|alpha - beta|/(k^2 - 1) of the Apollonius circle give alpha - c = k^2(beta - c) and k = R/|beta - c|.
concept_use.Diametrical form of circle: (z - z1)(zbar - zbar2) + conj = 0 is recognised as the circle on z1 z2 as diameter, giving centre 4+6i and radius 5.

key_step: Read the diametric circle (centre 4+6i, radius 5) and invert the Apollonius formulas: k = R/|beta - c| = 5, alpha = c + k^2(beta - c).
justification: Two ideas linked in the reverse direction (diametric form, Apollonius centre-radius relations / inverse points) with a numerical answer; average Advanced, near 2021-P1-Q16 (L3, recover parameters from a given circle).
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, locus and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, and the Hindi mirrors the English. Checked that 5+6i is inside C, so alpha and k > 1 exist and are unique, and verified the ratio 5 at two points of C. Answer 902, positive 3-digit integer. No change.
